_usage: jev_ask(state=<output of <skill-dir>/scripts/jev_state.py, unchanged, including its 'derived' facts>, questions=<this file's 'questions' with <_rules> replaced by _rules>). Questions are independent; every rule is in the question text, jev sees nothing else. jev has no scratchpad: arithmetic lives in jev_state.py's 'derived', not in this text. Re-measure with direct jev_ask runs on real states before changing any wording (see HANDOFF addendum 3).
_rules: Context: NMR relaxation-dispersion global fitting. Each hypothesis fits residues in groups; residues in one group share the global parameters kex and pB. In the state, each fit log entry has residues_on, global.red_chi2 (reduced chi-square of that group fit), preferred (global or individual), jackknife.rel_se_pct, and per_residue rows; the hypotheses_total_n_<n> object lists every hypothesis with its total AICc on the same total n: K1_global (all residues share one cluster), individual (every residue fitted alone), K<m>_global (m shared clusters), K<s>_plus_individuals_global (s shared clusters plus the residues in 'individuals', each fitted alone). Lower AICc is better. Decision rules, applied in order: (1) if the full fit has red_chi2 <= 1, the structure is K1 and any split is overfitting. (2) if the full fit has preferred=global and jackknife rel_se_pct of a few percent, the structure is K1. (3) a hypothesis is valid only if every one of its multi-residue group fits has preferred=global and rel_se_pct below about 5; single-residue fits are individuals and need no jackknife. (4) among valid hypotheses, the one with the lowest AICc is selected; never prefer a hypothesis that splits a group whose own red_chi2 <= about 1.1. (5) the selected structure is named by its hypothesis key: K<m>_global means K<m>; K<s>_plus_individuals_global means K<s>_plus_individuals. When the state has a 'derived' object, trust it: it was computed by code from the fits and lists, per hypothesis, valid (true/false by rule 3), delta_aicc_vs_K1 (negative = better than K1_global), and the full fit's gate (red_chi2_le_1, global_preferred_small_se); 'selected' is the lowest-AICc valid hypothesis by rule 4. Use the derived facts instead of recomputing arithmetic.

questions.question: <_rules> Rate the strength of evidence FOR the proposed split (K>1 or individuals) over a single global cluster.
levels: none: rule 1 or rule 2 resolves the structure as K1; no split is warranted
weak: the full fit fails rules 1-2, but no valid split hypothesis is present, or the best valid split lowers total AICc below K1_global by less than 2
moderate: a valid split hypothesis lowers total AICc below K1_global by 2 to 10
strong: a valid split hypothesis lowers total AICc below K1_global by more than 10

questions.question: <_rules> Which cluster structure do the rules select for this data?

options.K1: all residues share one cluster (rule 1 or 2 applies, or K1_global has the lowest valid AICc)
options.K1_plus_individuals: the selected hypothesis is K1_plus_individuals_global: one shared cluster plus individually fitted residues
options.K2: the selected hypothesis is K2_global: two shared clusters, no individuals
options.K2_plus_individuals: the selected hypothesis is K2_plus_individuals_global: two shared clusters plus individually fitted residues
options.K3: the selected hypothesis is K3_global: three shared clusters, no individuals
options.K3_plus_individuals: the selected hypothesis is K3_plus_individuals_global: three shared clusters plus individually fitted residues
options.K4_or_more: the selected hypothesis has four or more shared clusters

questions.question: <_rules> Would splitting the residues further than the selected hypothesis be justified? Yes when derived.selected is null and the full fit fails the gate (the single shared cluster is rejected), or when a multi-residue group of the selected hypothesis fails rule 3. No when the gate holds or every group of the selected hypothesis passes.
questions.yes_means: the current grouping is rejected and residues must be split further
questions.no_means: the selected grouping holds; further splitting is overfitting

questions.question: <_rules> Are additional fits needed before K can be decided? Yes exactly when derived.needs_more_fits is true, which code sets when derived.selected is null (the full fit fails the gate and no valid split hypothesis is present).
questions.yes_means: derived.needs_more_fits is true: more fits are required
questions.no_means: derived.selected names a hypothesis: the shown fits already decide K
